question: In CKD, anaemia develops primarily because failing kidneys produce insufficient erythropoietin, resulting in normocytic normochromic anaemia.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The primary cause of CKD anaemia is EPO deficiency — renal peritubular cells that produce EPO are progressively lost as nephron mass falls. The result is normocytic normochromic anaemia that worsens with declining eGFR.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. EPO deficiency is the dominant cause of CKD anaemia. The peritubular fibroblasts of the renal cortex synthesise EPO; their progressive loss drives normocytic normochromic anaemia. Other contributing factors include iron deficiency, uraemic toxin-mediated marrow suppression, and shortened RBC lifespan.
